title: SLA-weighted enterprise intake and safe-rollout prioritizer for model-catalog submissions
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: enterprise customers submit model variants, pin requests, and deprecation asks that require deterministic prioritization so we meet contractual SLAs, protect stability for paying customers, and keep catalog quality high. Current intake is ad hoc: PMs manually triage, engineering capacity is not always aligned to SLA-constrained requests, and legal/security checks are applied late in the cycle.

Goal: design and implement an SLA-weighted intake and prioritization rubric + safe rollout path for model-catalog items that: (1) produces a single numeric priority score for routing to fast-path vs standard lanes, (2) surfaces required compliance/security/legal checks up-front, and (3) automates a safe rollout sequence (shadow -> canary -> pinned exposure -> global) with clear bump/fallback rules and timelines.

Scope: intake form fields, scoring algorithm, lane definitions, approval gates, required artifact links, observability handoffs, and a rollout template that integrates with Console rollouts and Dedicated capacity reservations. Excludes infra work to provision Dedicated pools (ENG to implement via dependency).

Scoring overview (proposed): PriorityScore = Base*SLA_weight + ComplianceMultiplier + StabilityDeltaPenalty + CostDeltaFactor + CustomerStrategicBoost. We will normalize to a 0-100 scale and define thresholds: >=80 Fast-path (24-72h triage + expedited eval), 50-79 Standard (1-2 week eval window), <50 Deferred (sandbox or scheduled backlog).

Fast-path guarantees: triage initial response within 48 hours, eval orchestration started within 72 hours, canary rollout in customer sandbox within 10 business days.

Output: a template intake automation document (for Console + internal intake UI), a playbook for PMs/SEs on required evidence at each gate, and a release plan for a pilot with 3 enterprise customers.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form updated in internal intake UI with fields for SLA tier, regulatory requirements, data residency, customer-provided evals and cost delta estimates.
Automated priority score produced and stored as a field on the Linear ticket and surfaced in Console intake dashboard.
Routing rules implemented: score >=80 routes to 'Fast-path' queue and notifies SE + on-call eng; score 50-79 routes to 'Standard' queue; score <50 flags for sandbox scheduling.
Playbook published: step-by-step fast-path runbook including required legal/security checklists and signoffs.
Pilot with 3 enterprise customers executed and metrics captured: triage time, eval time, canary error rate, rollback frequency.
decision_notes: Enterprise SLA is the dominant signal: requests tied to contractual SLAs get a 2.5x weight in Base score.
Compliance/Regulatory items (data residency, export controls) apply a multiplier that forces manual legal/sec review before eval orchestration can start.
Pinned-version requests require a stability delta measurement: if new variant increases failure/regression risk by >8% on core evals, require a staged shadow period of min 14 days.
Cost delta above 1.4x (token/unit) reduces priority unless customer funds Dedicated reservation; include cost-offset checkbox in intake form.
Shadow trials should be the default safe-rollout for high-risk enterprise models; canary exposures limited to 5% of production tokens during pilot.
